entries.message: expected a component element and received {received}.
entries.fix: It adopts the element's own class `static styles` — `adoptStyles(this)`.
Pass a css`…` result, a string of CSS, or an array of those — a falsy entry is fine and is skipped, so `[base, dark && darkSheet]` works.

entries.message: expected a component element as the *second* argument and received {received}.
entries.fix: The order is styles first — `applyStyles(sheet, this)`.

entries.message: expected a template literal and received {received}.
entries.fix: It is a tagged template — write css`p { color: red }`, not css('p { color: red }').

entries.message: this engine has no `@scope`, so light-DOM `static styles` are hoisted to the document **unscoped** — every rule applies page-wide here and only to <{tag}> elsewhere.
entries.fix: Attach a shadow root to scope them everywhere, or write selectors that carry the tag.

entries.message: has no shadow root, and `::slotted()` only ever matches inside one — those rules do nothing here.
entries.fix: In light DOM you do not need it: slotted content is in the same tree, so an ordinary descendant selector reaches it. For a component that renders BOTH ways, write both — `::slotted(img), [part="body"] img`.
